title: Help to upgrade from XP to MZ

posts.author: PokerJersona5
posts.body:
Hello, I've been using RPG Maker XP for a while now to make Pokémon fangames using Pokémon Essentials.
I'm now developing unique games, and I'd like to know where the script editor is in MZ I can't seem to find it, if it's not there I'd like help with editing scripts.

posts.author: kirbwarrior
posts.body: MZ doesn't use scripts in the way that XP through VX Ace did. Instead, they have plugins that are more separate. There's all sorts of tutorials and help on the site, but it is going to be a LOT different since it's also done in a different coding language.

posts.author: TeiRaven
posts.body:
As Kirb said, "scripts" are only found in XP and VX/A. Starting with MV, the code you can use to change the behavior of the game is known as "plugins." Additionally, plugins are written in Javascript, not in Ruby like the scripts of old.
You can't edit the plugins directly in-engine. Just like any other resource, you have to edit them in other software and import them. I believe that you can adjust the things that the plugin is meant to change--such as turning features on and off--in-engine? But I'm the first to admit that I know very, very little about them, so I may not have that quite right.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
TeiRaven said:
you can adjust the things that the plugin is meant to change--such as turning features on and off--in-engine
Click to expand...
It depends on how the plugin has been written and what has been made as a public class.
(Sorry, to the programmers, I don't know what it's called in JS, I'm just referencing my tiny bit of programming in C# for Unity knowledge)
Generally speaking, however, yes, most plugins let you alter the plugin's function through the plugin manager or plugin command.
The plugin manager will let you control plugin parameters which affect how the plugin functions as a whole, while plugin commands will adjust certain limited parameter sets directly via an event command, allowing for changing of some plugin behavior mid game. Think of like a lighting system, the plugin command may allow you to enable or disable the lighting.
